attributes.description: Fires when at least 95% of a Supavisor pool's open connections are checked out, leaving almost nothing for the next client. Covers projects on the shared pooler, which emit no PgBouncer series at all.
attributes.name: [Supabase OTel] Supavisor pool exhausted

investigation_guide.blob:
## Supavisor Pool Exhausted

Supavisor is the shared, multi-tenant pooler fronting the database. It supports both session and transaction pooling, and the alert reports which mode is affected. With 95% or more of the open connections checked out, the pool has almost no capacity left for the next client.

### Triage Steps
1. Note the pooling mode. `session` mode pins a backend for the whole client session, so it exhausts far more easily than `transaction` mode; a workload in session mode that should be in transaction mode is a common cause.
2. Check whether the underlying Postgres connection budget is also near its ceiling — Supavisor cannot open backends that PostgreSQL will not grant.
3. Check query latency and long-running transactions. Connections held longer than necessary exhaust a correctly sized pool.
4. Confirm client behaviour with `supavisor_client_queries_count` and `supavisor_client_joins_ok` to distinguish a traffic increase from connections being held.

### Tuning
The rule fires at 95% checked out, so a small number of idle connections may still be reported — `Idle` is shown as context and a non-zero value does not contradict the alert. Note that `Pool Size` is derived from the connections that exist right now (`Checked Out` + `Idle`) rather than from a configured maximum, because Supavisor publishes no pool-size gauge. A very small pool therefore crosses 95% easily; raise the `Pool Size` floor in the query if that proves noisy. Supavisor series only exist when the shared pooler is in use, and they can be sparse; projects on the dedicated PgBouncer pooler produce no rows and the rule stays silent. Widen the window if your Supavisor scrape is intermittent.

esqlQuery.esql:
TS metrics-supabase.metrics.otel-*
// Supavisor gauges are per tenant / mode / node, so SUM() across series gives the pool
// totals for the tenant. Projects without the shared pooler emit none of these series,
// so the query returns no rows rather than a false breach.
| STATS
    `Checked Out` = SUM(LAST_OVER_TIME(supavisor_pool_connections_checked_out)),
    `Idle` = SUM(LAST_OVER_TIME(supavisor_pool_connections_idle)),
    `Active Connections` = SUM(LAST_OVER_TIME(supavisor_connections_active))
  BY resource.attributes.supabase_project_ref, attributes.tenant, attributes.mode
| EVAL `Pool Size` = `Checked Out` + `Idle`
| WHERE `Pool Size` > 0
| EVAL `Checked Out %` = ROUND(`Checked Out` / `Pool Size` * 100, 1)
// 95% of the open pool checked out. Pool Size is derived from live connections, so a very
// small pool crosses this easily; raise the Pool Size floor if that proves noisy.
| WHERE `Checked Out %` >= 95
| EVAL alert_instance = CONCAT(resource.attributes.supabase_project_ref, " / ", attributes.tenant, " / ", attributes.mode)
| SORT `Checked Out %` DESC
